title: FlashVSR official README
claims: FlashVSR v1.1 was released in November 2025 and v1 in October 2025; the README recommends v1.1.
The author reports approximately 17 FPS on 768x1408 video with one A100; this is an A100 method-level result, not a Colab/Wan paired benchmark.
The official project is primarily designed and optimized for 4x video super-resolution and strongly recommends 4x.
Block-Sparse Attention is reported correct with ideal acceleration on A100/A800, limited on H200, and unknown on RTX40/50 and H800.
The author warns that early third-party integrations omitting LCSA can visibly degrade high-resolution quality through aliasing/artifacts.

resources.precision: BF16 in official v1.1 full script

input_output_specs.crop: official full script uses 128-pixel target grid and center crop

audio_preservation: Official full script writes frames/video and does not document copying input audio.
measurement_scope: Author README claim on one A100; no L4/A100-40/80 split or host-RAM peak.
limitations: A100 kernel compatibility does not establish L4 fallback or speed. Third-party wrappers may omit LCSA and differ in quality.

title: FlashVSR v1.1 full inference script
claims: The script sets scale=4 and computes scaled dimensions, floors target width and height separately to a 128 multiple, then bicubic-resizes and center-crops each frame.
For video inputs it reads the input FPS and uses it when writing output; image-folder input defaults to 30fps.

The script appends four copies of the final frame, computes F as the largest value <= N+4 of the form 8n+1, truncates indices to F and passes F to the pipeline; it prints F-4 as a nominal target count but does not trim returned frames after inference.
The pipeline can set tiled=False for higher VRAM/faster operation or tiled=True for lower memory/slower operation; official full script uses tiled=False.

resources.resolution: target width/height each floored to 128 multiple

input_output_specs.frame_grid: 8n+1 after appending four repeated final frames

audio_preservation: No audio read/copy/mux code in the cited full script.
measurement_scope: Static code contract read at current main; actual decoded output frame count and PTS require a local probe.
limitations: The frame-index truncation can omit original tail frames for some N; the script has no post-inference trim or exact-duration assertion. A 2x path is not documented by this script.

title: FlashVSR-Pro independent implementation
claims: The repo is an independent reimplementation, not the official FlashVSR code release.
It adds audio-track preservation, DiT/VAE tiling, Docker/NVENC, and reflective padding to preserve exact output duration and Scale×input resolution according to the README.

Hardware claims are minimum 8GB for low-resolution tiled videos, 16GB+ recommended for high quality, 24GB+ for 4K, and 16GB+ system RAM recommended; minimum GPU is stated as RTX3060/3070 or similar Ampere/Ada/Hopper.
The CLI defaults to scale 2, but the README says original FlashVSR is primarily tested/recommended at scale 4; full mode is high quality/high VRAM, tiny and tiny-long use a lower-memory TCD decoder.
The README exposes tile size default 256, overlap 24, --keep-audio, --fps, --tile-dit and --tile-vae.

resources.gpu: Minimum RTX3060/3070 class claimed; A100/H100/H200 production focus

input_output_specs.crop: README claims reflective padding rather than crop
input_output_specs.frame_grid: README claims smart padding for 8n+1 and exact frame count

audio_preservation: `--keep-audio` explicitly copies input audio when present.
measurement_scope: Author implementation claims; no L4/A100-40/80 paired wall-time or quality result in the read README.
limitations: Independent fork may differ from official v1.1; exact duration/resolution, quality and low-VRAM figures are not independently verified here.

title: ByteDance-Seed SeedVR2 official README
claims: SeedVR2 is a one-step diffusion video restoration model; official quick start uses SeedVR2-3B and a target res_h/res_w.
One H100-80G is stated to handle 100×720×1280 video; four H100-80G support 1080p and 2K with sequence parallel size 4.

The official notice warns prototype performance may differ from the paper, and says heavy degradation/large motion can fail while lightly degraded 720p or 480p AIGC can be oversharpened or over-detailed.
Official code and weights are Apache-2.0.

resources.gpu: 1x H100-80G for 100 frames at 720x1280; 4x H100-80G for 1080p/2K

audio_preservation: Official script writes video frames with mediapy and does not document audio stream copying.
measurement_scope: Official resource statement, not an A100/L4 benchmark; no wall-time or host RAM.
limitations: Heavy-motion and light-degradation failures are explicitly documented; no identity-preservation guarantee and no native audio mux.

title: SeedVR2 3B inference script
claims: The script area-resizes each input to the requested res_h*res_w, allows upsampling because the model is trained for high resolution, clamps values and crops to 16-pixel divisibility.
The script pads the temporal sequence so `(t-1) % (4*sp_size)==0`, then trims generated samples back to original length before writing.
It preserves input FPS unless --out_fps is supplied and writes video via mediapy; output video has no audio-copy path in the cited code.

input_output_specs.temporal: 4n+1 after padding, then trim to ori_length

audio_preservation: No audio stream read or mux in the cited official script.
limitations: Output resolution is target-area based and aspect ratio/crop behavior must be probed for each clip; no identity/motion correction evidence.

topic: SeedVR2 ComfyUI models, BlockSwap and benchmarks
title: ComfyUI SeedVR2 Video Upscaler
claims: The wrapper exposes 3B/7B FP16 and FP8 model filenames and a standalone CLI; default model is 3B FP8 and default resolution width is 1072.
For GPUs under 24GB, the README says batch_size=1 is a workable no-temporal-consistency path, while batch_size=5 enables temporal consistency; larger batches need more VRAM.
BlockSwap can swap 0–32 blocks for 3B or 0–36 for 7B between GPU and CPU; more blocks save VRAM but slow inference.
On H100 93GB, 3B FP8 149 frames at 854x480→1920x1080 takes 361.22s (0.41 FPS); on RTX4090 24GB, 3B FP8 5 frames 512x768→1080x1620 takes 14.66s and 7B FP8 5 frames takes 46.23s with preserve_memory.

resources.workflow: SeedVR2 Video Upscaler node or inference_cli.py

audio_preservation: No audio handling is documented in the wrapper README/CLI contract.
measurement_scope: Author-maintained Comfy wrapper tables; no L4/A100-40/80 table.
limitations: Wrapper warns it consumes all VRAM even for 3B; 7B FP8 quality issues are noted in updates. H100/4090 data cannot be extrapolated to L4/A100.

title: SeedVR2-lite v1.5.8 standalone toolbox
claims: The README describes an independent standalone Windows/Web UI toolbox with 3B, 7B and 7B-Sharp models, FP16/FP8 and INT8-convrot/MXFP8/NVFP4 variants, and GPU BlockSwap.
Its model table lists SeedVR2-3B FP16 at minimum 16GB VRAM/~12GB memory, 3B FP8 at 8GB/~8GB, 7B FP16 at 24GB/~20GB and 7B FP8 at 12GB/~12GB; 7B-Sharp has the same FP16/FP8 rows.
The README says FP8 is a storage format and FP8/FP16 inference speed is approximately the same; BlockSwap, resolution and frame count control speed, with 2048² about 3–4x slower than 1024².
Portable package requirements are Windows x64, NVIDIA GPU >=8GB and >=15GB disk; video repair requires separately installed FFmpeg.

resources.gpu: NVIDIA CUDA; no named A100/L4 run
resources.resolution: Tool allows configurable image/video output; 1024² vs 2048² cost note

input_output_specs.audio: FFmpeg required but preservation contract not stated

audio_preservation: No explicit keep-audio/mux behavior in the cited README; FFmpeg is required for video repair.
measurement_scope: Independent tool README, including claimed 2026-09-02 real-machine validation; no reproducible L4/A100 wall-time table.
limitations: Third-party tool explicitly disclaims affiliation with ByteDance; its memory/quality claims are not official model-card qualification. No exact frame grid or identity/motion metric.

title: Real-ESRGAN official README
claims: The official model set includes RealESRGAN_x4plus, realesrnet-x4plus, realesrgan-x4plus-anime, realesr-animevideov3 and small anime-video models.
Python inference supports arbitrary final outscale, tile options and FP16 default; NCNN portable executables run without CUDA/PyTorch and expose scale 2/3/4 and tile size.
The project is explicitly for image/video restoration but its Python video script is the executable video path; framewise image models do not provide a temporal consistency guarantee.
The repository is BSD-3-Clause; model weights and external dependencies remain separately scoped.

resources.gpu: NVIDIA/AMD/Intel portable NCNN or CUDA PyTorch

input_output_specs.crop: tile stitching in NCNN can introduce block inconsistency

audio_preservation: The official video script copies the original audio stream when present; no audio synthesis.
measurement_scope: Official usage/model contract; no L4/A100 wall-time or VRAM table.
limitations: Framewise restoration can flicker or drift across frames; no official identity/motion correction or temporal consistency claim.

topic: Real-ESRGAN video audio mux and frame contract
title: Real-ESRGAN official video inference script
claims: The script probes input video width, height, average FPS, frame count and whether an audio stream exists.
The writer sets output width/height to input dimensions multiplied by outscale and uses input FPS unless --fps overrides it.
When audio exists, ffmpeg output uses the audio stream with acodec=copy while encoding video; the script therefore preserves an existing track rather than generating a new one.
The video path supports frame processing through a Reader/Writer loop, optional tiling, and multiple workers that split input video segments with ffmpeg.

resources.frames: input frame count read by ffprobe

input_output_specs.frame_count: input frame count used by Reader

audio_preservation: Existing audio is passed through with `acodec=copy`; generated audio is unsupported.
measurement_scope: Static official script inspection; no run.
limitations: No explicit PTS/variable-frame-rate guarantee; subprocess splitting uses ffmpeg -async 1, so timestamp behavior should be probed on real clips.

title: ECCV2022-RIFE official README
claims: The official CLI supports exp=1 for 2x interpolation and exp=2 for 4x interpolation, plus arbitrary-timestep image interpolation.
The README reports 30+ FPS for 2x 720p interpolation on a 2080Ti; this is a 2080Ti author measurement, not L4/A100.
For 4K input, the README recommends optical-flow processing scale=0.5; if disordered patterns appear, it suggests scale=2.0.
The `--fps=60` slomo path explicitly removes audio.
audio_preservation: The official --fps=60 route removes audio; remux must be separate.
measurement_scope: Author 2080Ti 720p 2x statement and static CLI contract; no L4/A100 timing.
limitations: Interpolation can fail or repeat frames for dissimilar endpoints; no identity or motion repair guarantee. Main code check POST15: default exp/video mode has conditional built-in source-audio transfer; the README audio-loss note applies to explicit FPS mode, not all interpolation.

title: RIFE issue #185: interpolation failure on dissimilar frames
claims: A user reports that image-to-image morphing sometimes produces no interpolation: in a 64x test, 63 frames were identical to input 0 and the final frame resembled input 1.
The report asks whether very dissimilar frames trigger an interpolation failure; no general fix is recorded in the issue.
measurement_scope: Single community issue report; no attached benchmark table.
limitations: Historical failure report; use as a known failure mode, not a current universal behavior claim.

title: MMAudio official README
claims: MMAudio generates synchronized audio from video and/or text using a synchronization module.
The official large_44k_v2 demo reports around 6GB GPU memory in 16-bit mode; default CLI duration is 8 seconds and default sampling is 25 steps.
CLI input is a video path plus prompt; official output is FLAC and an MP4 composition. Longer/shorter durations may work, but large deviation from 8 seconds can lower quality.
The CLIP encoder resizes to 384x384, Synchformer resizes the short edge to 224 and center-crops, CLIP operates at 8 FPS, Synchformer at 25 FPS, and input below 25 FPS is duplicated.
Known limitations include unintelligible speech-like sounds, unprompted background music and poor handling of unfamiliar concepts. Code is MIT; checkpoints are CC-BY-NC 4.0.

resources.gpu: No named GPU; official 16-bit memory claim
resources.resolution: Input conditioning resized/cropped to 384x384 and 224 short-edge path

input_output_specs.fps: CLIP 8 FPS; Synchformer 25 FPS with low-FPS duplication

audio_preservation: Generates a new audio track; does not preserve an original audio stream as source audio.
measurement_scope: Official README memory/contract claim; no L4/A100 wall-time.
limitations: Video input is centrally cropped for conditioning; generated audio may be semantically wrong, speech-like noise or music. Checkpoint license is non-commercial CC-BY-NC 4.0.

title: MMAudio demo.py
claims: The CLI exposes --video, --prompt, --duration, --num_steps, --variant and --skip_video_composite; default variant is large_44k_v2, duration 8.0 and steps 25.
When a video is supplied, the script saves audio to a FLAC file and, unless --skip_video_composite is set, calls make_video to create an MP4 with generated audio.
The script logs max CUDA memory allocation after generation, but does not publish a fixed per-GPU wall-time table.
audio_preservation: Generated audio is composited into MP4; original source audio is not passed as an input audio track.
limitations: No source A/V mux comparison, no PTS policy beyond the library's make_video implementation, no L4/A100 timing.

title: ComfyUI-MMAudio custom nodes
claims: The repository provides ComfyUI nodes to use MMAudio, with installation into custom_nodes and model loading from ComfyUI/models/mmaudio.
It links safetensors model files and uses NVIDIA BigVGAN v2 for the 44k mode; example_workflows are included in the repository.

input_output_specs.output: audio node / video composition depends on graph

audio_preservation: Wrapper README documents generation nodes and model paths, but does not state original-audio preserve/mux behavior.
measurement_scope: Repository setup inspection; no run or resource table.
limitations: Community wrapper may diverge from official CLI and requires an independent ComfyUI environment.

title: Official RIFE inference_video.py audio transfer conditions
claims: When --fps is omitted, output FPS defaults to input FPS times 2**exp and fpsNotAssigned is true.
Video input, non-PNG output and fpsNotAssigned trigger transferAudio after interpolation.
transferAudio first attempts lossless stream copy and can fall back to AAC; failure can leave a silent video. Explicit --fps or PNG output skips this merge.
limitations: Code-level preservation contract, not an executed audio/PTS test in this survey.
